image_observation: A lower remnant meets the deeply impressed right-hand frame. The second frame is too incomplete to trace.
The right-hand animal panel ends at an upright ridge. The other print is poorly resolved near the painted accession number.
Two transverse ridges divide very short relief remnants. Their intervening boundaries do not show a directional crossing.
Views A1–2 and A3–4 show several levels and shallow relief. The surviving boundaries are incomplete across both views.

The long line A3 starts below a sharp rim at the lower edge of A2. The junction could record a later press but no trackable crossing was identified. Frenez 2020 figs. 7 and 9 provide additional views.
A2 has a short dark lip in the lower field of A1. Wear and cracks obscure which features the lip interrupts.
The lower text field meets the right-hand area on a broken and cracked face. Inset A2 bis does not disambiguate the seam.
Frenez and Tosi 2005 p. 75 describe three superimposed impressions. The split views show a boundary on A3 without a continuously traceable earlier feature.
Both views preserve partial text and sharp ridges. Cracks and surface loss obscure a junction.
Two rows flank a sharp ridge. No continuous earlier edge demonstrably ends against it.
Two text zones meet at a thick shadowed lip. The lower diamond and strokes are readable but the lip alone does not determine order.
Lower relief begins at a shadowed rim. Adjacent surface damage makes truncation uncertain.

A2 has a sharp upper-left corner and a continuing rim below A1's incomplete lower field. A1 before A2 is plausible. Concretions and fractures make the crossing ambiguous. Published overlap in Frenez and Tosi 2005 p. 75 and additional photo in Frenez 2020 fig. 7.
Relief occupies neighboring inclined zones. The central transition is worn and offers no clear crossing.
Different views display the two zones. The shared boundary cannot be traced between them.
The two worn relief zones meet by a raised seam and damaged side. Neither supplies a diagnostic interrupted feature.
The lower row is visibly clearer. The rough strip between rows provides no directional crossing.
The large rectangular depression meets another battered zone. No continuous earlier border can be followed to a truncation.
A and F show impressions on faces described as orthogonal by Frenez and Tosi 2005 p. 80. No diagnostic crossing is visible at their junction.
Two legible rows sit at a strong horizontal step. Indistinct relief at the step leaves the order open.
A framed lower print with a long line sits against the worn upper area. The boundary offers no diagnostic visible truncation.
The lower text zone begins under a long straight edge. Upper perimeter and relief are obscured by wear.
The sharp curved strip between upper A1 and lower A2 also coincides with a break-like change in surface. Frenez 2020 figs. 1 and 7 show another angle. No secure sequence.
Both views show stepped surfaces with worn relief. There is no traceable crossing.
The square upper animal print and smaller lower text remnant are separated by a broken strip in both views.

The lower stamp A3 has an uninterrupted upper and left rim across the field beneath A2's text. A3 after A2 is the strongest reading of the boundary. Frenez and Tosi 2005 p. 79 describe preservation of the earlier legends on this object. The upper A1/A2 boundary is left unscored.
The lower framed impression meets a highly fractured upper field. There is no traceable crossing. Plate caption says A 1–3 while the published 2020 table counts two.
The upright step and lower-left print appear adjacent but the contact is shadowed. The painted 1170 is modern.
The upper print has a bottom edge above a worn lower zone. No traceable truncation is visible.
Deep depressions remain but the available plate does not resolve their edges or sequence. Plate caption says A 1–4 while the published 2020 table counts five.
D1, D2 and E are partial views with uneven relief. They do not resolve a shared crossing.
